messages:
Maya R: Hey infra team — want to sync on an idea: build a combined 'regional card telemetry' Grafana dashboard that fuses ECC/Xid/network-flake signals + capacity headroom so SREs can triage flaky cards faster and we can tune SLOs by region. rough proposal below, PTAL.

Sam: +1. can we see example queries and the alerting windows you had in mind?

Maya R: Sure — thinking of two layers:
- short-term alerts (5–15m windows) for immediate drains/fails
- medium-term regressions (6h) for rolling bake/ops review
- daily summaries for capacity planning and cost tradeoffs

Sample PromQLs (prototype panels):
```
# ECC errors per GPU (5m rate)
sum by (gpu_serial, region) (rate(nv_gpu_ecc_errors_total[5m]))

# Xid errors, normalized per 1e6 kernels (5m)
sum by (gpu_serial, region) (rate(nv_gpu_xid_errors_total[5m]))
/
(sum by (gpu_serial) (rate(nv_gpu_kernel_calls_total[5m])) + 1e-6) * 1e6

# Flaky-card inference failures (app-level)
sum by (gpu_serial, region) (rate(inference_failure_total{reason=~"OOM|CUDA_ERROR|XID"}[5m]))

# Regional capacity headroom gauge
(available_gpus{region="$region"} / total_gpus{region="$region"}) * 100
```

Maya R: In the dashboard UI we'd show a heatmap (region x time) for ECC/Xid rates, a table of top-10 noisy GPUs (rank by Bayesian shrinkage score, see below), and per-rack aggregation so infra can correlate with rack-level telemetry (temps/power). Also a time-shifted panel to spot regressions vs baseline.

Ingrid: What do you mean by Bayesian shrinkage score? sounds heavy.

Maya R: Lightweight — basically combine counts with a prior so low-count GPUs aren't over-ranked. formula (pseudo):
```
score = (observed_errors + alpha * mu) / (observed_ops + alpha)
```
where mu is fleet-wide error-rate prior, alpha is pseudo-count (we'll tune per-metric). Means GPUs with 2 errors in 1 minute but tiny ops won't bubble up.

Noah: For alerts, recommend two thresholds:
- Alert A (page): sustained score>thresh_A over 10m and ECC/Xid spike > X (critical)
- Alert B (ticket): elevated score over 1h but below critical — auto-create a triage ticket, no page

ops-bot: created alert gpu-card-ecc-spike-dev with severity=page for team=infra (just a test)

Sam: We need to align SLOs with product requirements. Proposal: regional GPU availability SLO 99.5% monthly for each prod region, with an objective to keep mean time to detection < 10m for ECC/Xid spikes and mean time to drain < 30m for high-confidence flakes.

Maya R: Agree. Also propose an economic knob: keep a regional hot-spare of 3% of capacity or min 4 gpus, whichever is higher. tradeoff: higher spare reduces evictions impacting customer throughput but increases costs. We should simulate with last-90d eviction traces.

Ingrid: Can we add a panel showing "cost vs spare" curve? e.g., expected lost throughput if spare < X vs monthly GPU cost delta. That will help product decisions.

Maya R: Yes — plan: run a Monte Carlo using historical card-failure inter-arrival and region demand to estimate tail risk. I'll share notebook.

Sam: Ops question — how do we avoid alert noise from scheduled maintenance or transient driver upgrades? We see spikes whenever kernel/drivers roll.

Maya R: We add a maintenance tag to kube nodes and enrich telemetry: ignore alerts for GPUs in nodes with label maintenance=true for the window. Also add a driver-upgrade suppression window: if fleet-wide driver version changes > 50% in 30m, suppress noisy alerts for 1h and create a maintenance ticket to review.

Noah: Nice. Also suggest a "card rehab" workflow: automatic soft-drain + 2 test workloads run (memtest, light inference) and if pass, put back; if fail, schedule replacement. Should be part of runbook.

Maya R: Agreed. Draft runbook bullets:
- Detection: alerts (A/B)
- Auto-soft-drain on Alert A (quiesce pods, migrate stateful if needed)
- Run self-test (30m) and collect logs
- If persistent errors or Xid>threshold -> mark for replacement + schedule tech ops
- If tests pass -> re-enable and track 48h stability metric

Ingrid: What about the Grafana panels for regional SLO reporting? We need a per-region ledger: uptime %, incidents, avg detection time, avg drain time, cost delta. This will feed weekly Site-Health review.

Maya R: I'll prototype a dashboard with sections: Overview (SLOs), Hot GPUs (ranked), Heatmaps (errors), Capacity (headroom + spare), Cost-impact curve, Recent incidents (inc link + ticket id). Expect to link to incidents channel for one-click drill.

Sam: Will we version dashboards and roll out via infra-cfg repo? prefer Terraform-managed grafana-dashboards so we can do PRs and rollbacks.

Maya R: Yes — plan to put JSON into infra-grafana/dashboards/gpu-telemetry.json and add alert rules in infra-alerts. Will start with dev region for 48h evaluation.

ops-bot: deployed dashboard gpu-telemetry-dev to grafana-dev (preview url: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/gpu-telemetry-dev)

Noah: Action items:
- Maya: push prototype PromQL + dashboard JSON to PR by EOD Wed
- Sam: draft SLO wording and oncall paging policy by Fri
- Ingrid: build cost-vs-spare sim and add panel mock
- Ops-bot: wire alert A/B to pagerduty/test-runs in dev

Maya R: thanks all — please react with :thumbsup: if you agree with the plan, or drop a quick dissent. I’ll iterate on the PR with alpha=5 for the shrinkage priors and initial thresholds: page if score>0.005 and Xid rate > 50/min per GPU.

Sam: :thumbsup:
Ingrid: :thumbsup:
Noah: :thumbsup:
